columns.rationale: distinct_count 3322 equals the table's row_count 3322 and null_rate is 0.0, so tailnum uniquely identifies each aircraft record (e.g. N10156, N102UW, N103US).

All sample_values (1956.0, 1959.0, 1963.0, ...) are integral despite the DECIMAL(38,9) landed type, so cast to INTEGER; null_rate is 0.021072 (70 nulls) so the column is retained as nullable rather than imputed.
distinct_count is 3 with distinct_values Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft, and null_rate is 0.0, so this low-cardinality category column is required.
distinct_count is 35 with sample_values like AIRBUS, BOEING, BEECH, BELL, and null_rate is 0.0, so manufacturer is kept as a required text field.
distinct_count is 127 with samples such as 172E, 310Q, 421C showing free-form alphanumeric model codes, and null_rate is 0.0, so model is kept as required text.
distinct_values are exactly 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, all integral, so cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER; null_rate is 0.0 so the column is required.
sample_values (2.0, 4.0, 5.0, ... up to max 450.0) are all integral counts of seats, so cast to INTEGER; null_rate is 0.0 so required true.

distinct_values (90.0, 95.0, ... 432.0) are integral so cast to INTEGER, but null_rate is 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), so the column is sparsely populated and retained as nullable rather than dropped or imputed.
distinct_count is 6 with distinct_values 4 Cycle, Reciprocating, Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet, Turbo-prop, Turbo-shaft, and null_rate is 0.0, so engine type is kept as a required category.
is_airbyte_metadata is true, marking this as a capture-tool identifier rather than a business column, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true with a single constant value 2026-09-02T23:26:22 across all rows, confirming it is a pipeline timestamp, not business data, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true and distinct_values shows a constant empty object {}, confirming it carries no business information, so it is dropped.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact-duplicate removal is required.
tailnum has distinct_count 3322 exactly equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so it plausibly identifies one row per aircraft and is declared the grain.

year, engines, seats, and speed all land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample and distinct_value observed (e.g. engines 1.0-4.0, seats 2.0-450.0, speed 90.0-432.0) is integral, so all four are cast to INTEGER.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows null); nulls are retained rather than imputed per cleanup policy.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), making it a sparsely populated column; it is retained nullable rather than dropped since some aircraft do carry a value.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.

purpose: This table provides cleaned, typed reference data on individual aircraft (by tail number) including manufacturer, model, engine configuration, and capacity, intended to feed downstream flight-analytics joins that enrich flight records with aircraft characteristics.
usage: Join to flight fact tables on tailnum, the declared grain; expect year and speed to be nullable (year ~2% null, speed ~99% null) so handle missing values explicitly rather than assuming presence, and treat engines/seats/year as INTEGER after the DECIMAL-to-INTEGER cast.
limitations: speed is populated for only about 0.7% of rows (null_rate 0.993076) so it is unreliable for broad analysis; year is missing for about 2.1% of rows; no duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was applied; all airbyte capture-metadata columns were dropped and are unavailable downstream.
